DONE for batched result reads. The transport-buffer half remains P7.2's by explicit assignment; see the boundary note at the end.

This succeeded on the second attempt because the first attempt established what was actually blocking it. That finding was the useful part: the protocol was never the hard bit — the await loop was.

STEP 1, committed separately (ec6f83b): RemoteAwaitDriver now owns the awaiting policy — exponential backoff, the 1-in-6 accounting cadence, tolerance of transient blindness, and the deadline. RemoteTaskHandle.await supplies only a tick. All 50 ssh tests passed unchanged across that refactor, including the timeout, tolerance and accounting paths, which is the evidence the semantics survived.

Without this, a batch poller would have been a SECOND awaiting implementation reimplementing all four policies. This epic has already fixed two bugs caused by exactly that pattern — three hand-written terminality classifiers (A2) and two independent constructions of one durable handle (D2) — so building a third instance of it to close a bead was not defensible.

STEP 2: AgentMethod.ReadResults with codecs reusing the per-ref ones, so the batch shape is an array wrapper rather than new domain encoding. The agent handler is deliberately the SAME per-ref read, looped: the server does no new work and the entire saving is transport. One failed read fails the group, because a partial answer would leave the caller unable to tell which refs were even attempted.

SshAgentApi.readResults guards the frame budget: maximumBytes bounds EACH result, so a group is admitted only when maximumBytes * groupSize fits the negotiated typed-result budget. An oversized group is a protocol failure, never a truncated answer.

STEP 3: RemoteBatchHandle.await now reads every still-pending element in ONE exchange per tick, driven by the same RemoteAwaitDriver the single handle uses. Two properties worth recording:
- It FALLS BACK to the per-element path when the group does not fit the negotiated frame. A refusal to batch must never become a refusal to await.
- A lost round trip yields AwaitTick.Blind, so the driver rides it out exactly as the single path does rather than abandoning a wait with hours left.

Together with G2's ceiling the scale story is now coherent: G2 bounded how many exchanges may be in flight, G3 reduced how many there are. A 100-element batch went from 100 SSH processes per tick to one.

Verification: existing RemoteBatchSuite exercises batch awaits end-to-end against a loopback agent and passes unchanged, so the batched path is genuinely in use rather than merely present. 2 new codec tests pin ordering as the correlation and reject an empty group. Full suite 434 green on Scala 3.3.8 AND 3.8.4, zero warnings under -Werror, scalafmt clean.

BOUNDARY, unchanged and deliberate: the ByteVector transport-buffer migration stays P7.2's (bd-01KYNA5EAA733KTPSK7M1V1JWZ), which cites FrameCodec's `buffered ++ input` as its own motivation. Doing it here would design the buffer twice. P7.2 is now unblocked in a way it was not when written — its gate P7.3 is closed, and the public shape has settled through D1-D5.
